text:
Matthew Poitras keeps scoring in small doses. The 22-year-old center has 4 goals and 7 points in 15 games while playing under ten minutes a night, which works out to 2.95 points per 60 minutes, a first-line rate from a fourth-line role.

Some of that is real. His rate of chances is up on what he managed in his brief stay last season, and his five-on-five share of expected goals, the quality of chances, sits at 53.4%. Some of it is not: four goals on 19 shots is a 21% shooting rate, and our range for him centres closer to 14%. He's also cooled, with one goal in his last ten games while his minutes slipped by almost two a night.

The bigger frame is what Boston wants him to be. He was a 95-point playmaker in his last OHL season at Guelph, and the Bruins have now lost three straight. A team searching for offense has a cheap place to look, if they trust him with more than nine minutes.
